So Demopolis law firm actually reached out to Salesforce because they had a lot of documents that they were receiving from their personal injury cases where they would get a lot of hospital forms and documents that were stored.

But not only is it that initial data extraction that they had to do, these cases are ongoing. So they receive documents as time passes, so that they receive via email and then IP helps extract that data so that that's basically the overview of why Demopolis uses IDP, and I'll maybe leave it to Kailash to give another little overview about the use case and how it's helped them with their operational efficiencies.

content.text:
Sure. Thanks for the overview. Checking. So what we have done, corner, for Demopolis law firm in particular is all the intake of their cases. Let's say that they come in with a case from the beginning to scan their ID to have the data entered into Salesforce for a basic contact creation before even the matter is created. A matter is a case inside the Salesforce legal side.

So the crash reports, the police witness reports, then the medical records that they submit, all of these files they submit as a zip file. So earlier, what the staff or the paralegal team used to do is that the case managers used to get all of these documents in PDF. They used to unchip and then enter all of these data into Salesforce.
But now we have built a custom code that a customer LWC component that accepts this zip file. Then it unzips it. It splits the documents into different documents because they give them as a single huge PDF, so we split them to make sure that they are split exactly into different documents and then identify which document type it is.
All the prompts written and IDP for each of these document types, it extracts that data and fills that. Salesforce. So what happens now is the case intake is gone from probably more than four or five hours of work into probably minutes of work. When they submit the document.

So it covers almost 70 different document types that come in. We have worked with files that are close to 600 pages together. IDP performs best up to 50 pages. So what we do is we identified the whole 500-600 pages document, split them into individual docs. We have written custom code to identify exactly where the document starts and where the document ends and then split them into different files once it enters all the data into Salesforce. They have a secured SharePoint folder where all of these individual documents are uploaded back to SharePoint, so that way the whole manual data has been reduced.

They can review it if they have any issues. They go there, they change it and then they approve it. Once they approve it, then only the data goes and is injected into Salesforce.
So that way there is a case manager review and then approval, then injection into Salesforce.

We don't want these long-running processes inside MuleSoft. So we gave all the split files to sit inside SharePoint and run through when each of the files is pushed back and then it starts processing the next.
So we vote a batch limit of five files at a time and then slowly move forward with the next ones.
